clue.text: Opportunist must change side section of church

indicators.note: the sides are right and left, so changing side swaps the letter for one with the letter for the other

parts.note: a chancer is someone who takes any opportunity going

explanation.surface: A self-serving churchgoer is told to move pews to the other side of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The final R (right) of the opportunist becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Retired elderly Democrats welcoming play?

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters are read going backwards up the column
welcoming means taking something in, so the letters are held within the clue's own words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Older retired Democrats welcome a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: this is one kind of play.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedy is a humorous play, so it is one example of a play.

clue.text: Nearly fall exposed atop second stone

indicators.note: in a down answer atop puts this piece above the next ones
exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters are removed

parts.note: the inner letters of fall
a mo is a moment, a second
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A rock nearly toppled from its exposed perch on another stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost and nearly are synonyms, both meaning not quite.

clue.text: Senator taking over maybe holding small insignia

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the senator's name

parts.note: Cato the Elder, the Roman senator
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a farm is a landholding, maybe signalling an example
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A politician's takeover of a small holding gets a badge of office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' looks like a container signal, but is land held, with 'maybe' marking it as one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat of arms is the heraldic emblem of a family or institution, a form of insignia.

clue.text: Decision reversed about one shade

indicators.note: reversed means read in the opposite direction, end to start
about means surrounding, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: a call is a decision, as a referee's call
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A ruling is overturned over one colour choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple colour, named after the flower, so one shade.

clue.text: Run ahead of runner filming item on the road

indicators.note: being ahead of something means coming before it, so the first part leads the second

parts.note: to dash is to run
a runner in crosswords is often a river; the Cam flows through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A jogger is caught on video by a camera out on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like a jogger but is a river, which runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashcam is a camera mounted on a car's dashboard that records the road ahead while driving.

clue.text: Exclusion of French people serving time

parts.note: de is French for of
barmen serve drinks
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: French prisoners serving a sentence are shut out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving time' suggests prison, but the people serve drinks and time is a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Debarment is the act of barring someone from something, so exclusion.

clue.text: Climbing archer becomes vexed

indicators.note: in a down answer climbing means going upwards, so letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: Eros, the god of love, shoots arrows

explanation.surface: An archer scaling a wall gets annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore in informal use means angry or annoyed, the same as vexed.

clue.text: Fill bird with suspicion leaving first of bread

parts.note: a crow is a bird

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: doubt is suspicion

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the first letter of bread

explanation.surface: Stuffing a bird, wary of losing the breadcrumbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fill bird' suggests stuffing poultry; fill is the definition, in the sense of packing a space.
explanation.definitionFit: To crowd out is to fill a space so fully that others are pushed away.

clue.text: Fools putting metal into skip

indicators.note: putting is placing, which together with the later word into tells where the metal goes
putting one thing into another places it inside that other thing

parts.note: to skip something is to miss it out
lead is a metal

explanation.surface: Pranksters throw scrap metal into a rubbish skip.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip in Britain is a large open bin for building rubbish; here it is the verb, to miss out.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead someone is to deceive them, which is what one does when one fools them.

clue.text: Reptile mass rounded up by degrees

indicators.note: being rounded up by something means being surrounded and enclosed by it

parts.note: two university degrees, MA (Master of Arts) and BA (Bachelor of Arts)
M is the abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A snake gathered into a pen, perhaps gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By degrees' reads as 'gradually', but the degrees are two qualifications either side of the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mamba is a fast, venomous African snake, and snakes are reptiles.

clue.text: Tough hunter briefly tails dog with American

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short, so its final letter is lost
to tail something is to follow behind it, so this piece comes after the next one named

parts.note: short for Labrador
Orion is the hunter of Greek myth and the constellation
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A hunter's hound and an American companion make for a difficult chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tails' reads as a noun but is a verb: the shortened hunter follows the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Laborious describes work that is hard and demanding, so tough in the sense of arduous.

clue.text: County being used for two musical events creates upset

indicators.note: one letter group serving two words at once means it is written only once where the words overlap

parts.note: a disco and a concert are both musical events
CO is the abbreviation for county

explanation.surface: A county's venue double-booked for two gigs causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The disco ends in CO and the concert begins with it, so the shared county abbreviation is written once at the join.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert someone is to unsettle or fluster them, the verb sense of upset.

clue.text: Overheard pin-up in need of occupation

indicators.note: something overheard is caught by ear, so the word's sound matters rather than its spelling

parts.note: a pin-up is a star or idol whose picture goes on a wall

explanation.surface: Eavesdropping on a poster model who is out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means unemployed or inactive, lacking work to do, so in need of occupation.

clue.text: Band in denim on air rocking

indicators.note: rocking means shaking about, so these letters are jolted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock group in denim plays on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' is the definition at the start, not part of the image of a group dressed in denim.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron Maiden is a famous British heavy metal group, so a band.

clue.text: Tablet possibly crushed in part of theatre?

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several possible arrangements, so these letters may be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
something crushed into powder has been ground

explanation.surface: A pill crushed up in the wings of a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is a theatre of war, not a playhouse; the question mark flags the shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleground is a site of fighting, and a theatre of war is made up of such areas.

clue.text: Yummy sides of hummus in overly large volume

parts.note: too means excessively

indicators.note: in says the selected letters go inside the next piece

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two outer letters, first and last

parts.note: the first and last letters of hummus

explanation.surface: Tasty edges of a dip, in far too big a helping.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome means pleasant to eat, delicious, so yummy.

clue.text: Crab Lane excited one attached to Hull?

indicators.note: excited letters are agitated and stirred up, so they fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A street in the Yorkshire port of Hull gets excited.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is the city, a port in Yorkshire; with a lower-case h it is a ship's hull, which the capital letter disguises.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnacle is a marine crustacean that fixes itself to rocks and ships' hulls.

clue.text: Shrewd relative with a pest repellent? On the contrary

parts.note: fly is British slang for knowing or sharp
pa is father
per means a, as in fifty pence a kilo

explanation.surface: A canny relative recommends an insect repellent, or perhaps the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' turns the definition inside out: the answer attracts pests instead of repelling them.
explanation.definitionFit: Flypaper is sticky paper that lures insects and traps them, the opposite of a repellent.

clue.text: Essential books on a large capital left inside

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the books follow everything else
inside says the following piece sits within the capital just named

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
Lima is the capital of Peru
port is the left side of a ship
NT is the New Testament, a set of Biblical books

explanation.surface: Reading matter about a big city, with something left behind in it, is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: The books, listed first, come last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: All-important means of the greatest importance, so crucial or essential.

clue.text: Nameless Serbian spreading disease

indicators.note: spreading things out scatters them, so the letters land in another order
nameless means without a name, so the letter for name is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An unnamed person from Serbia is passing on an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabies is a viral infection of the nervous system passed on by animal bites.

clue.text: Rugged banks of Tay supporting shorebird

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: the knot is a wading bird of the sandpiper family

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Tay, the Scottish river

explanation.surface: Wading birds along the rough edges of a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotty wood is gnarled and lumpy, so knotty can mean rough or rugged in texture.

clue.text: Track camera around base part of neck

indicators.note: turned around, a word is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: to pan is to swing a camera to follow a moving subject
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A film crew moves its camera to the back of someone's neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' is the mathematical constant e, the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: The nape is the back of the neck, a specific part of it.

clue.text: Reconsider narrow range accepted by family

parts.note: narrow means thin

indicators.note: to be accepted by something is to be taken into it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: kin are one's family
an Aga is a British brand of range cooker

explanation.surface: A family takes in a slim cooker after second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a large cast-iron kitchen stove, the archetypal British range cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: To think again is to review a decision and possibly change it, so to reconsider.

clue.text: Small part of new clue originally dropped

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: the original, first letter is dropped down to the end of the word

parts.note: a hint is a clue

explanation.surface: A bit of a fresh crossword clue was cut at first.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, dropped means moved down, so the first letter goes to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninth is one of nine equal parts of a whole, so a small fraction of it.

clue.text: Short unit surfaced with unknown element

indicators.note: something short is missing its end, so the last letter goes
in a down answer, surfaced with means topped by, so this piece goes on top

parts.note: z is an algebraic unknown
an inch is a unit of length

explanation.surface: A small unit is paved over with an unknown chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a metallic chemical element, atomic number 30.

clue.text: Sign of cold sailors eating fruit with tons cut

indicators.note: eating something means taking it inside, so the sailors surround the fruit

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: something cut has a part taken away, here the letter named just before

parts.note: an apricot is a fruit
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Chilly sailors snack on fruit, with a sign of the zodiac in view.
explanation.walkthrough: The fruit loses its T, then sits inside the sailors' RN, after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn is the goat, one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Fissure on ledge essentially gathered snow

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the fissure follows the other piece
essentially points to the essence or heart of a word, its central letter

parts.note: the middle letter of ledge
a rift is a crack or fissure

explanation.surface: A crack opens on a mountain ledge where snow has built up.
explanation.definitionFit: A drift is a bank of snow heaped up by the wind, snow that has gathered in one place.

clue.text: Painful condition of area, unusually red

indicators.note: unusually says these letters appear in an unusual order and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary, is a famous red

explanation.surface: A doctor notes a patch of skin is strangely red and sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a colour but is a communist, Che Guevara.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is pain in the ear, an uncomfortable medical complaint.

clue.text: Openness in perfect animal enclosure

parts.note: to hone a skill is to perfect it
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: Transparency is found in an ideal pigpen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' reads as an adjective but is the verb, to perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Honesty is frankness and candour, an open, truthful manner.
